name: Partial correlation
when: 要判断某个因子在其他因子同时在场时的独立影响，且因子之间本身相关
when_not: 要看非线性关系 → 用偏依赖图或加样条；要看因果 → 需要实验或工具变量
assumptions: The relationship between the response and each factor is approximately linear over the sampled region.
No unobserved confounding variable is present. Without this, a partial correlation is an association, not an effect.
No near-perfect collinearity exists among the factors, which would make the partial correlation unstable and prone to sign changes.
breaks_when: Fewer than about 30 observations: the asymptotic critical value $z_{\alpha/2}/\sqrt{n-k-1}$ no longer holds, and the significance judgement becomes unreliable.
Collinearity is strong: the partial correlation can exceed the zero-order correlation and flip sign under small resampling.
Non-linearity is real: the partial correlation understates the influence, and the understatement cannot be detected from the coefficient alone.
refs: Pearson, K. (1896). Mathematical contributions to the theory of evolution. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A, 187, 253-318.
Cohen, J. (1988). Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences, 2nd edition. Lawrence Erlbaum.
